clue.text: US politician's dismissed in the matter of bar-keeper

indicators.note: dismissed means sent away, so this short piece is taken out of the politician

parts.note: a Republican is a member of one of the two main US parties; the 's is 'is'
re means concerning, in the matter of

explanation.surface: A clue about an American politician being sacked in some affair involving a barman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissed' removes RE ('in the matter of') from REPUBLICAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A publican runs a pub, so is its landlord and barman.

clue.text: Scientist using speed of light in basis of theory

indicators.note: in places the light-speed symbol within the word for a basic principle

parts.note: a plank is one of the basic principles of a political platform or theory
c is the physics symbol for the speed of light

explanation.surface: A physicist building a theory on the speed of light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts C inside PLANK.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Planck was the German physicist who founded quantum theory.

clue.text: Summer-house much liked before, nothing less

indicators.note: less means without, so the letter for nothing is dropped from the charade

parts.note: someone much liked is beloved
O, the zero shape, means nothing
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A summer-house that was much liked in the past, nothing more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' takes O ('nothing') out of BELOVED + ERE.
explanation.definitionFit: A belvedere is a garden pavilion or summer-house built to give a view.

clue.text: I will have opinion about note that's a demand for payment

parts.note: to have a voice is to have an opinion or say

explanation.surface: Someone stating their opinion about a bill that demands payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts VOICE round N, after I.
explanation.definitionFit: An invoice is a bill sent to request money owed.

clue.text: A King and Queen like a tapestry

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
R is short for regina, Latin for queen
as means like

explanation.surface: A royal couple resembling figures woven into a hanging.
explanation.definitionFit: An arras is a wall hanging woven with pictures, named after the French town.

clue.text: Authoritarian head of school bamboozled, we hear

indicators.note: head of picks the opening letter of the word school
we hear means the word for bamboozled is taken by its sound

parts.note: to be bamboozled is to be tricked

explanation.surface: A stern headteacher who, rumour says, has been fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of' gives S; 'we hear' turns TRICKED into the sound TRICT, so S + TRICKED said aloud is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A strict person insists on rules being obeyed, as an authoritarian does.

clue.text: Cheers in favour of order where drink is supplied

parts.note: ta and cheers are both informal British thanks
pro means for, in favour of
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A toast and a call for order where drinks are served.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British slang for thank you; OM, the Order of Merit, is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A taproom is the bar of a pub where beer is served from the tap.

clue.text: Independent? Cost makes you aggrieved

parts.note: a rate is a charge or cost

explanation.surface: A question about whether going it alone is worth the price that annoys you.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone irate is angry, as one feels when wronged.

clue.text: Your rates, nothing less, may be redefined by Government department

indicators.note: redefined suggests the letters are given a new shape, a rearrangement
less means minus, so the nothing letter is dropped from your

parts.note: O, the zero shape, means nothing

explanation.surface: Your local rates may be changed by a ministry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' drops O ('nothing') from YOUR, leaving YUR; 'may be redefined' shuffles YUR + RATES.
explanation.definitionFit: The Treasury is the UK ministry that manages public finance.

clue.text: Doctor in South American country receiving new issue

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the country holds the doctor

parts.note: Chile is a country on South America's Pacific coast

explanation.surface: A doctor working in Chile who takes on a new case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' looks like a matter or edition, but here it is the legal word for offspring; 'receiving' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue in law means offspring, sons and daughters.

clue.text: Worldwide description of hopelessness?

explanation.surface: A remark that despair is found in every country.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means everywhere, and also messy or confused, as a hopeless effort is.

clue.text: Believes listing of TV workers

explanation.surface: Someone who trusts the names that roll at the end of a programme.
explanation.definitionFit: To credit something is to believe it; the credits list a show's cast and crew.

clue.text: Nothing in school punishment is showing an element of pride

indicators.note: in places the zero letter inside the punishment

parts.note: lines are sentences a pupil must copy out as a penalty
O, the zero shape, means nothing
is shortened to 's

explanation.surface: A pupil given no punishment showing a little pride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts O inside LINES, then S for 'is' as in 's. A pride is a group of lions.
explanation.definitionFit: A pride is a group of lions, so a female lion is one member of it.

clue.text: It's the last thing you'd expect to find in a calendar

definitions.text: It's the last thing you'd expect to find in a calendar

parts.words: It's the last thing you'd expect to find in a calendar
parts.note: seems to mean something surprising, but literally names the final month on the page

explanation.surface: Something you would be amazed to see printed on a calendar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The last thing you'd expect' is an idiom for something surprising; read literally it is the final month.
explanation.definitionFit: The year's twelfth month comes at the end of every calendar.

clue.text: Library book I loaned out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A library book I lent to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges I + LOANED to ODLEIAN. The Bodleian is Oxford University's library.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bodleian is the main research library of the University of Oxford.

clue.text: Man amassing money is a man without time ()

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the time letter is removed

parts.note: Mister is the title for a man

explanation.surface: A man hoarding cash is a man with no time to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes T ('time') from MISTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser hoards wealth and spends as little as possible.

clue.text: Supplier of dressing case about to go bust

indicators.note: to go bust means to break, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A case of salad dressing about to burst open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go bust' rearranges CASE + ABOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A sauceboat is a jug for pouring gravy or sauce over food.

clue.text: Writer taking half a month over index, say

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits above the second
half a takes the front half of the eleventh month's name

parts.note: an index is one kind of list

explanation.surface: An author spending a fortnight compiling an index.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half a' takes NOVE from NOVEMBER; 'over' puts it above LIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A novelist writes long works of fiction.

clue.text: The end point in some games

indicators.note: in shows the letters run inside the words some games

explanation.surface: The finishing stage reached in certain sports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' hides the answer in sOME GAmes.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, so stands for the end.

clue.text: Old North American upset over one investing in his currency

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits above the second
upset in a down clue turns the letters upside down, so read backwards
investing means surrounding or clothing, so the numeral goes within the coin

parts.note: the cent is the North American's coin
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An old American angry about the coins he holds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his currency' refers back to the North American, whose coin is the cent; 'upset' turns its piece upside down in this down clue, and 'over' stacks it on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient means very old.

clue.text: This creature is around? That's wrong!

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone told a prehistoric beast is still alive, and objecting.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks whether the beast is still alive and answers no; 'That's wrong' is the anagram signal on the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinosaur is an extinct prehistoric reptile, a creature no longer living.

clue.text: Martyr's last words? Crikey!

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise set beside a martyr's dying words.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone me is a British exclamation of surprise; a martyr stoned to death, like St Stephen, might say it literally.

clue.text: Lorry gets cold in polar region- 11.

indicators.note: gets means takes in, so the lorry receives the cold letter

parts.note: an artic is an articulated lorry

explanation.surface: A lorry driver getting chilly in the far north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' puts C inside ARTIC; ARTIC is British for an articulated lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arctic is the region round the North Pole.

clue.text: Middle of leg a girl cut-the pain

indicators.note: Middle of takes the central letter of the word leg
cut means shortened, so the girl's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Rachel is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl's leg wound causing pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle of' gives E from leg; 'cut' trims RACHEL to RACHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Earache is pain inside the ear.

clue.text: Soldiers game to join up again

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a tie is a cup match, a game

explanation.surface: Soldiers playing a match together again.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British army corps; a tie is a knockout cup match.
explanation.definitionFit: To retie is to fasten or knot again.

clue.text: Settler, an individual requiring external support

indicators.note: requiring external means the single unit sits within, with the support outside

parts.note: a pier is a supporting pillar
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A settler on his own needs outside help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'requiring external support' reads as needing outside help, but splits so that 'support' is the outer piece and 'requiring external' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer is among the first to settle new territory.

clue.text: Pensioner clutching it turns up in paved area

indicators.note: in a down clue turns up means the letters are read bottom to top
clutching means holding, so the pensioner holds the word it

parts.note: OAP is an old-age pensioner

explanation.surface: An elderly person holding something appears on a terrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses the whole container (OITAP) in this down clue, which is why the letters read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A patio is a paved outdoor area by a house.

clue.text: Desperately completing the tour?

explanation.surface: Rushing frantically to finish a holiday trip.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means as a final option when all else fails; literally, at the final holiday town on a tour.

clue.text: Number departed during the year

indicators.note: during means within, so the leaving word sits inside

parts.note: t' is the dialect form of the, as in northern English
departed means went

explanation.surface: A remark on how many people died over the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' puts WENT between T and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty is the number after nineteen.

clue.text: Items wrongly pocketed by medic's servant

indicators.note: pocketed by means placed inside, so the doctor holds the shuffled items

parts.note: doc is short for doctor, a medic

indicators.note: wrongly means the letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A servant's belongings mistakenly taken by the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of 'Items' gives MESTI; 'pocketed by' says that goes inside the doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic is a household servant.
